supporting_observations.claim: WS-MFISCHER-01 made repeated connections to the explicit proxy at 10.55.20.30:8080 during the alert window. A series is spaced roughly five minutes apart: 13:45:47, 13:51:03, 13:56:17, 14:01:08, and 14:06:20 UTC.
The cited periodic records identify connections to the internal proxy over HTTP, but do not identify the external HTTPS destinations or the originating process.

The observed cadence is compatible with the inventory description of the approved LedgerLink updater checking about every five minutes, but the available records do not establish that LedgerLink generated these connections.

The proxy records show that destination-level HTTPS details are available for some later activity: at 14:16:17 the proxy logged a browser request to OneDrive. Those later records do not identify the destinations of the periodic connections in the alert window.

known_telemetry_limitations: For the cited periodic sessions, the supplied network records show the workstation connecting to the proxy but do not include corresponding destination-level proxy events or process attribution.
The later OneDrive proxy records identify a destination and browser user agent, but are outside the alerted activity and cannot be used to attribute the earlier periodic sessions.
claims_not_established: Whether the periodic sessions were generated by the approved LedgerLink updater, another legitimate application, or an unauthorized process.
Which external hosts or URLs the periodic sessions contacted, and what content was transferred.
Whether the activity was related to the scheduled password rotation or workstation patching.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve full proxy CONNECT, request, and TLS inspection logs for WS-MFISCHER-01 from 13:20–14:20 UTC, especially for the periodic sessions.
Obtain endpoint process-to-network telemetry for those timestamps to identify the process responsible.
Check LedgerLink installation, updater, and update-check logs for the same period, and compare their destinations and timing with the proxy records.
Review IT patch execution and change records, including activity originating from WS-IDOYLE-01, for the relevant window.
unrelated_findings: At 14:19:43–14:19:45 UTC, the proxy logged max.fischer browsing Google Drive, an unapproved cloud-storage service. This is outside the alert's 13:30–14:10 periodic-connection window and should be handled separately.

The Google Drive proxy activity is associated with Firefox process 4824 in the supplied endpoint network records; it does not establish that Firefox or Google Drive generated the alerted periodic sessions.
